learning_objective: Build a strong foundation in Java syntax, data, operators, control flow, methods, object-oriented programming, collections, and exceptions.
how_to_use_this_guide: For every lesson, read the explanation, run the code, and review the points_to_remember.

subtopics.name: Java Basics and Program Structure
subtopics.explanation: Java source code is written in classes. Execution normally begins in the main method. The compiler converts source code into bytecode, and the JVM runs that bytecode.
points_to_remember: The public class name must match the file name.
main is the standard entry point.
Java is case-sensitive.
Statements normally end with a semicolon.

subtopics.name: Comments and Naming
subtopics.explanation: Comments are ignored by the compiler. Naming conventions make code easier to read.
points_to_remember: Use camelCase for variables and methods.
Use PascalCase for classes.
Use UPPER_SNAKE_CASE for constants.

subtopics.name: Variables and Data Types
subtopics.explanation: A variable is a named storage location with a type. Java has eight primitive types and reference types such as String, arrays, and objects.
points_to_remember: Primitive types store simple values; reference variables refer to objects.
Use L for long and f for float literals.
Local variables must be initialized before use.
null is allowed for reference types, not primitive types.

subtopics.name: Primitive Types
subtopics.explanation: byte, short, int, and long store whole numbers; float and double store decimals; char stores one character; boolean stores true or false.
subtopics.code:
byte a = 1; short b = 2; int c = 3; long d = 4L;
float e = 1.5f; double f = 2.5; char g = 'J'; boolean h = true;
points_to_remember: int is the usual whole-number type.
double is the usual decimal type.
Use long when int is not large enough.

subtopics.name: Constants with final
subtopics.explanation: final prevents a variable from being assigned again. static final fields are commonly used as constants.
subtopics.code:
static final double TAX_RATE = 0.18;
final int DAYS_IN_WEEK = 7;
points_to_remember: A final variable can be assigned only once.
Constants are usually named in uppercase.
final prevents reassignment, not object mutation.

subtopics.name: Type Casting and Conversion
subtopics.explanation: Widening conversion moves a value to a type with a larger range and is usually automatic. Narrowing requires an explicit cast and may lose data.
points_to_remember: Casting double to int truncates; it does not round.
Narrowing can lose data or overflow.
Use Integer.parseInt to convert numeric text to int.
Use String.valueOf to convert a value to text.

subtopics.name: Operators
subtopics.explanation: Operators calculate values, compare data, assign results, and build conditions. Parentheses make precedence explicit.
points_to_remember: Use parentheses when precedence is not obvious.
Do not compare strings with ==; use equals.
Integer division discards the fractional part.
Do not confuse = assignment with == comparison.

subtopics.name: Arithmetic Operators
subtopics.explanation: + adds, - subtracts, * multiplies, / divides, and % returns the remainder.
points_to_remember: Integer division returns an integer.
Division by zero throws an exception for integers.
Remainder is useful for even/odd checks.

subtopics.name: Relational Operators
subtopics.explanation: Relational operators compare values and return boolean: ==, !=, >, <, >=, and <=.
points_to_remember: A comparison produces true or false.
== compares primitive values.
Use equals for object content such as String.
= assigns a value; == compares values.

subtopics.name: Logical Operators
subtopics.explanation: && means AND, || means OR, and ! reverses a boolean value.
points_to_remember: && and || use short-circuit evaluation.
&& skips its right side when the left side is false.
|| skips its right side when the left side is true.

subtopics.name: Assignment Operators
subtopics.explanation: Assignment stores values. Compound forms combine assignment with arithmetic, such as +=, -=, *=, /=, and %=.
points_to_remember: = assigns a value.
Compound assignment combines an operation and assignment.
Compound assignment includes an implicit cast back to the variable type.

subtopics.name: Unary Increment and Decrement
subtopics.explanation: ++ increases by one, -- decreases by one, and unary + or - indicates a numeric sign.
points_to_remember: Postfix uses the old value before changing it.
Prefix changes the value before using it.
Avoid complex expressions with multiple increments.

subtopics.name: Ternary Operator
subtopics.explanation: The ternary operator has the form condition ? valueIfTrue : valueIfFalse and returns one of two values.
subtopics.code:
int marks = 72;
String result = marks >= 40 ? "Pass" : "Fail";
points_to_remember: Both branches should have compatible types.
Use if/else when the expression is hard to read.
Ternary is an expression that returns a value.

subtopics.name: Bitwise Operators
subtopics.explanation: &, |, ^, and ~ work on individual bits of integral values.
points_to_remember: Bitwise operators are useful for flags and masks.
& and | differ from short-circuit && and ||.
Bitwise operators work on integral types.

subtopics.name: Shift Operators
subtopics.explanation: << shifts bits left, >> shifts right while preserving the sign, and >>> shifts right while filling with zeroes.
points_to_remember: Left shift commonly multiplies by powers of two.
>> preserves the sign bit.
>>> inserts zeroes from the left.

subtopics.name: Control Flow
subtopics.explanation: Control-flow statements choose between paths or repeat a block of code.
points_to_remember: Conditions must evaluate to boolean.
Use braces for readable blocks.
Keep branches small and focused.

subtopics.name: if, else if, and else
subtopics.explanation: if runs when true, else if checks another condition, and else handles remaining cases.
points_to_remember: Conditions are checked top to bottom.
Only the first matching branch runs.
Order overlapping ranges carefully.

subtopics.name: switch Statement and Expression
subtopics.explanation: switch selects code based on one value. Arrow syntax avoids accidental fall-through, and switch expressions return values.
points_to_remember: Include default for unexpected values.
Traditional cases need break to stop fall-through.
Labels must match the switch value type.

subtopics.name: for, while, and do-while
subtopics.explanation: for is useful when the iteration pattern is known, while checks before each iteration, and do-while always runs at least once.
points_to_remember: Update loop state so the loop can finish.
while may execute zero times.
do-while executes at least once.

subtopics.name: break, continue, and enhanced for
subtopics.explanation: break exits a loop, continue skips to the next iteration, and enhanced for visits every element.
points_to_remember: Use break and continue sparingly.
Enhanced for is ideal for reading every element.
Use an indexed loop when you need positions.

subtopics.name: Methods
subtopics.explanation: Methods package reusable behavior. A method accepts parameters and may return a value or use void when it returns nothing.
points_to_remember: Java passes arguments by value.
A return statement must match the declared return type.
Give methods one clear responsibility.
static methods belong to the class; instance methods belong to objects.

subtopics.name: Parameters, return values, and void
subtopics.explanation: Parameters are local inputs. A return value sends a result to the caller; void means there is no returned value.
points_to_remember: Arguments follow parameter order.
A void method can use return; to exit early.
Validate inputs when invalid values break the method contract.

subtopics.name: Method Overloading
subtopics.explanation: Overloading uses one method name with different parameter lists. The compiler chooses the matching signature.
subtopics.code:
static int add(int a, int b) { return a + b; }
static double add(double a, double b) { return a + b; }
points_to_remember: Return type alone cannot overload a method.
Parameter count, types, or order must differ.
Overloading is compile-time polymorphism.

subtopics.name: Arrays
subtopics.explanation: An array stores a fixed number of values of one type. Indexing starts at zero and length gives the number of elements.
points_to_remember: The last index is length - 1.
Array size cannot change after creation.
Invalid indexes throw ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException.
Arrays can contain primitives or references.

subtopics.name: Creating and Updating Arrays
subtopics.explanation: Arrays can be initialized with values or created with a fixed length. Elements are changed through indexes.
points_to_remember: A new int array starts with zero values.
A new boolean array starts with false values.
A new reference array starts with null values.

subtopics.name: Two-Dimensional Arrays
subtopics.explanation: A two-dimensional array is an array whose elements are arrays, useful for tables and grids.
subtopics.code:
int[][] grid = {{1, 2}, {3, 4}};
System.out.println(grid[1][0]);
points_to_remember: Use array[row][column].
Java supports jagged arrays.
Nested loops commonly visit every cell.

subtopics.name: Strings and StringBuilder
subtopics.explanation: String is immutable, so its contents cannot change after creation. StringBuilder is mutable and efficient for repeated text changes.
points_to_remember: Use equals for String content comparison.
String methods return new strings.
Use StringBuilder for repeated concatenation in a loop.
String literals may be stored in the String pool.

subtopics.name: Common String Operations
subtopics.explanation: String provides methods for length, searching, extracting parts, changing case, and removing whitespace.
points_to_remember: substring uses inclusive start and exclusive end.
Many methods are case-sensitive.
Check indexes before charAt or substring.

subtopics.name: StringBuilder
subtopics.explanation: StringBuilder changes one character sequence with append, insert, delete, and reverse.
points_to_remember: Call toString when an actual String is required.
StringBuilder is not synchronized.
It is especially useful inside loops.

subtopics.name: Object-Oriented Programming
subtopics.explanation: OOP models programs with classes and objects. Its core ideas are encapsulation, inheritance, polymorphism, and abstraction.
points_to_remember: A class defines state and behavior; an object is an instance.
Keep fields private and expose controlled behavior.
Prefer composition when inheritance is not a true is-a relationship.

subtopics.name: Classes, Objects, and Constructors
subtopics.explanation: A class is a blueprint. A constructor initializes a new object and has the class name with no return type.
points_to_remember: new creates an object and calls a constructor.
this refers to the current object.
Constructors are not inherited.

subtopics.name: Encapsulation and Access Modifiers
subtopics.explanation: Encapsulation protects internal state. public, protected, package-private, and private define visibility.
points_to_remember: private members are accessible only inside their class.
Use methods to validate state changes.
Expose only behavior that callers need.

subtopics.name: Inheritance and Polymorphism
subtopics.explanation: extends creates a subclass. A parent-type reference can point to a child object, and overridden behavior is selected at runtime.
points_to_remember: A class has one direct superclass.
Use @Override to verify overriding.
The reference type controls accessible members; the object type controls overridden behavior.

subtopics.name: Abstract Classes and Interfaces
subtopics.explanation: An abstract class can share implementation and declare abstract methods. An interface defines a contract that classes implement.
points_to_remember: Use implements for an interface.
A concrete class must implement required methods.
A class can implement multiple interfaces.

subtopics.name: Static, Wrapper Classes, and Enum
subtopics.explanation: Three useful Java features: static members belong to the class, wrapper classes represent primitive values as objects, and enums define a fixed set of constants.
points_to_remember: Static methods cannot directly access instance fields.
Autoboxing converts primitives to wrappers and unboxing converts back.
A wrapper reference can be null; a primitive cannot.
Use enum for a fixed set of choices.

subtopics.name: Static
subtopics.explanation: The static keyword makes a variable or method belong to the class rather than to individual objects.
points_to_remember: Static members belong to the class.
A static method can be called using the class name.
Static methods cannot directly access instance variables.
Static variables are shared by all objects of the class.

subtopics.name: Wrapper Classes
subtopics.explanation: Wrapper classes represent primitive data types as objects, such as Integer for int and Double for double.
points_to_remember: Every primitive type has a corresponding wrapper class.
int → Integer, double → Double, char → Character, boolean → Boolean.
Autoboxing converts a primitive into a wrapper object.
Unboxing converts a wrapper object back into a primitive.
Wrapper references can be null, but primitives cannot.

subtopics.name: Enum
subtopics.explanation: An enum defines a fixed set of named constants, making it useful when a variable can have only specific values.
points_to_remember: Enum represents a fixed set of constants.
Enum values are accessed using the enum name.
Use enum instead of arbitrary strings for predefined choices.
Enum values can be used with switch statements.

subtopics.name: Input and Output
subtopics.explanation: System.out prints to standard output, while Scanner reads formatted input from the console.
points_to_remember: Use nextLine for a complete line and nextInt for an integer token.
After nextInt, consume the remaining newline before nextLine.
Close resources when finished.
Validate input before using it.

subtopics.name: Exception Handling
subtopics.explanation: Exceptions represent abnormal situations. try contains risky code, catch handles a matching exception, finally performs cleanup, and throw/throws communicate errors.
points_to_remember: Catch specific exceptions before general ones.
Do not silently ignore exceptions.
Use try-with-resources for AutoCloseable resources.
Checked exceptions must be caught or declared.

subtopics.name: throw and throws
subtopics.explanation: throw sends an exception now. throws declares that a method may pass an exception to its caller.
points_to_remember: Use exceptions for exceptional situations.
Exception messages should explain the problem.
Preserve the original cause when wrapping exceptions.

subtopics.name: Collections Basics
subtopics.explanation: Collections store groups of objects with flexible sizes. List preserves order, Set prevents duplicates, and Map stores key-value pairs.
points_to_remember: Collections store reference types, so use wrappers for primitives.
List permits duplicates and keeps order.
Set stores unique elements.
Map keys are unique.
Use interface types on the left when possible.

subtopics.name: List
subtopics.explanation: List is an ordered collection that allows duplicate elements. ArrayList is a common implementation of the List interface.
points_to_remember: List maintains insertion order.
List allows duplicate elements.
ArrayList is commonly used when frequent access by index is required.

subtopics.name: Set
subtopics.explanation: Set is a collection that does not allow duplicate elements. HashSet is a common implementation of the Set interface.
points_to_remember: Set does not allow duplicate elements.
HashSet does not guarantee insertion order.
Use Set when uniqueness of elements is required.

subtopics.name: Map
subtopics.explanation: Map stores data as key-value pairs. HashMap is a common implementation of the Map interface.
points_to_remember: Map stores data as key-value pairs.
HashMap does not guarantee insertion order.
Keys must be unique, while values can be duplicated.
Check whether a key exists when a lookup may return null.

subtopics.name: Packages, Imports, and Debugging
subtopics.explanation: Packages organize classes and prevent naming conflicts. Imports allow short names. Debugging uses compiler messages, stack traces, logs, and breakpoints to find causes.
points_to_remember: The package declaration comes before imports.
A stack trace shows the exception and call path.
Read the first relevant application line in a stack trace.
A debugger lets you inspect variables line by line.

practical_projects.description: Practice input, operators, methods, and switch with a four-operation calculator.
practical_projects.algorithm: Read two numbers, select an operation, validate division by zero, and print the result.

practical_projects.description: Practice Random, Scanner, conditions, loops, and counters.
practical_projects.algorithm: Generate a target from 1 to 100 and repeat guesses until the target is found.

practical_projects.description: Practice strings, loops, methods, and boolean return values.
practical_projects.algorithm: Use two pointers for palindrome checking and trial division up to the square root for prime checking.
